statement: A disclosure detector and the policy classification that makes its findings actionable must be decided together. In this incident a standing public-surface scan reported closed-name hits for a week while the governing classification remained provisional, so the alarm had no authorized disposition. Once the operator rules a category closed, record the concrete instances in the denylist, remove the names from every mutable public surface, preserve published records through visible errata rather than silent history edits, and verify the exact deployed scanner returns zero. A category-only disclosure boundary is incomplete because each new instance otherwise starts unclassified. Move condition: after the coordinated Cejel and Alfred PRs merge, anchor to both origin/main squash commits only after verifying their diffs preserve standing-constraints byte parity and the complete public-surface scan reports zero closed-name findings.
